newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares revive after export data shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares revive after export data shake-up.

text.p: Singapore shares recovered a shade from disappointing May non-oil export figures but the mood of investors remained cloudy, dealers said on Friday.
The market sought refuge in stronger performing blue chips after the market took a dive, and bargain-hunting led the index back into positive terrain.
"It was quite bad after the release of the export data but people saw good values and came in to buy," a remisier said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 5.47 points at 2,008.44 on volume of 110 million lots. The broader market was weaker with losers outpacing gainers 178 to 146.
The bleak export outlook, with nominal exports year-on-year down one percent, instead of up 3.5 percent as a Reuter survey on Thursday had forecast, dampened trading enthusiasm.
Small stocks were favoured earlier in the day, but interest also waned after the export report, dealers said.
The most active stock, Van der Horst, reversed its uptrend to brush new lows at Singapore $2.11. It ended 36 cents lower at S$2.22, failing to recoup Thursdays' losses.
SIA traded sideways to end only five cents up at S$7.20, despite its announcement of an Asia-Pacific alliance.
